title: Order-one rigidity, consecutive carrier tests, and a two-ended seam ledger
question: can the final-three investigation be strengthened by an exact divisor theorem, actual canonical microsteps, and endpoint harmonic data?

verdict.conclusion: order-one Hadamard rigidity closes the appended-counterterm route more generally; the natural symmetric dyadic completion remains order one only by adding an infinite boundary divisor. Actual N=14 to N=15 and one-to-two-carrier numerical refinements fail positive-axis interlacing. The Blaschke marker admits an exact two-ended Poisson product and an unweighted seam determinant, but no prime or theta theorem yet forces its endpoint product to one.

completedLedgerRigidity.sameDivisorTheorem: if two entire functions of order at most one have the same zeros with multiplicity, their quotient is exp(a+bs), so their logarithmic second derivatives are identical
completedLedgerRigidity.consequence: no order-one re-completion with the xi divisor can change the central curvature; cancelling the dyadic term must reappear in another ledger component rather than leave every reservoir empty
completedLedgerRigidity.boundaryDivisorDescription: zeros lie at s=2 pi i k/log 2 and s=1+2 pi i k/log 2 on both strip boundaries; using the reciprocal replaces them by poles
completedLedgerRigidity.gammaDuplicationCheck: Gamma(s/4)Gamma(s/4+1/2)=2^(1-s/2)sqrt(pi)Gamma(s/2); the power of two is exp(linear in s) and has zero logarithmic curvature, so duplication does not supply the missing quadratic counterterm
completedLedgerRigidity.status: the curvature can be moved only by raising order or adding a zero/pole boundary reservoir

canonicalInterlacing.comparisonDomain: positive critical-line ordinates through height 30; using the full symmetric line would create a trivial central-pair obstruction for any two even functions
canonicalInterlacing.consequence: failure is present both in the actual consecutive N=14 to N=15 deficit transition and when the second fully admitted theta carrier is added; it is not an artefact of comparing distant N=14 and N=20 stages
canonicalInterlacing.limitation: these are robust argument-principle and quadrature diagnostics for the implemented canonical completions, not a rigorous interval-arithmetic theorem for the exact untruncated integral
canonicalInterlacing.remainingTarget: a redesigned refinement with a proved Sturm, Hermite-Biehler, or total-positivity structure

twoEndedSeamLedger.finiteHeightDeterminant: Delta_T=product over zero-orbit representatives with |gamma|<=T of cos^2(pi eta)
twoEndedSeamLedger.extendedLimit: Delta=lim_T Delta_T exists in [0,1] because every factor is at most one; Delta=1 exactly under RH, although it may collapse to zero when the unweighted defect sum diverges
twoEndedSeamLedger.coerciveInfimum: inf_a P_a(+1)P_a(-1)=sech^2(sup_a d_seam), equal to one exactly under RH
twoEndedSeamLedger.blaschkePhaseMeaning: P_a at a boundary point is the boundary phase derivative of the elementary Blaschke factor, so horizontal displacement is the product of its phase slopes at the two seam endpoints
twoEndedSeamLedger.fourBranchIdentity: for 0<|eta|<1/2, 4 epsilon(eta/2)<epsilon(eta), because with c=cos^2(pi eta/2), c^2-(2c-1)=(c-1)^2>0
twoEndedSeamLedger.advance: unlike the quadratic residue, the exact seam defect still contracts under as many as four half-displacement descendants
twoEndedSeamLedger.remainingFailure: the full Blaschke phase derivative is a sum of Poisson kernels and diverges at the accumulation endpoints; recovering the per-zero two-ended product requires a renormalized endpoint factorization not supplied by current prime data
twoEndedSeamLedger.sufficientMissingTheorem: derive from the completed prime ledger or canonical theta kernel that the two-ended endpoint product has infimum one, or that it is invariant under a globally defined halving return

exactAdvances: upgraded the counterterm obstruction to same-divisor order-one Hadamard rigidity
located the natural symmetric dyadic reservoir explicitly on both strip boundaries
tested a genuinely consecutive stage and a literal one-carrier refinement on the positive spectral axis
converted the seam norm into an exact product of two endpoint Poisson phase slopes
constructed an unweighted seam determinant and defect that remain sensitive to escape
proved the seam defect contracts even under four descendants at half displacement
remainingObligations: prove a renormalized two-ended endpoint identity from prime or theta data
or construct a different canonical refinement with rigorous interlacing
or supply an internal completed-ledger identity without shifting curvature into a boundary divisor
combinedAssessment.status: the seam ledger is sharper and branch-robust, but arithmetic control remains missing and RH is not proved
